Purified Yashada was melted and vigorously triturated with Apamarga powder until converted to fine powder and heated further under an earthen pot.

Jarita Yashada was triturated with Kajjali (mercury–sulphur mixture), levigated with Aloe vera and lemon juice, pelletized, sealed in earthen pot, and subjected to 2 cycles of incineration to obtain yellowish Yashada Bhasma.

Jarita Yashada was triturated with Kajjali (mercury–sulphur mixture), levigated with Aloe vera and lemon juice, pelletized, sealed in earthen pot, and subjected to 2 cycles of incineration to obtain yellowish Yashada Bhasma.

Purified Swarnamakshika was mixed with purified Gandhaka, levigated with lemon juice, formed into pellets (chakrikas), sealed in Earthen container, and subjected to repeated incineration (cow dung cake heating) to obtain Swarnamakshika Bhasma.

Purified Swarnamakshika was mixed with purified Gandhaka, levigated with lemon juice, formed into pellets (chakrikas), sealed in Earthen container, and subjected to repeated incineration (cow dung cake heating) to obtain Swarnamakshika Bhasma.
Shodhita Tuttha was levigated with Citrus Medica Juice, formed into pellets, dried, sealed in earthen pot, and subjected to three successive heating cycles to obtain Tuttha Bhasma.

Purified Tuttha was mixed with equal amounts of purified sulphur and borax, ground with Lakucha (Artocarpus hirsutus) juice to form a paste, shaped into small pellets, dried, sealed in earthen containers, and heated in three controlled heating cycles until Bhasma was obtained.
Purified Mukta Shukti pieces were placed between layers of Aloe vera pulp in a sealed earthen pot and heated under controlled high-temperature conditions (Gajaputa) for the initial calcination.

The calcined material was ground with fresh lemon juice into a uniform paste to form pellets, dried, sealed in earthen containers, and reheated under controlled high-temperature conditions for two additional calcination cycles until the final Bhasma was obtained.
